candidate_relations.reason: The biopsy shows reactive B-cell follicles with CD20-positive, BCL-2-negative germinal centers rather than cutaneous T-cell lymphoma; the delayed UVA reaction and cheilitis support actinic prurigo.
No muscle disease or characteristic dermatomyositis eruption is described, and it does not account for the specified actinic prurigo with cheilitis.
The chronic pruritic papules, lower-lip cheilitis, delayed UVA erythema, and biopsy findings are not diagnostic of psoriasis.
There are no blisters, acantholysis, or immunologic findings supporting pemphigus; it does not represent actinic prurigo with associated cheilitis.
No flaccid bullae, mucosal erosions, suprabasal acantholysis, or supporting immunofluorescence findings are reported for pemphigus vulgaris.
The record lacks follicular hyperkeratotic papules, orange-red plaques, palmoplantar keratoderma, or islands of sparing typical of pityriasis rubra pilaris.
